then.text: {greeting} Our Whit Friday winners! The cup's on the piano. The piano is not ours, so don't lean on it.
Cornet, tuba, drum, and you. That's a band! Right, coats on. The contest march starts at the top of the village.
Oh, heck. The Thornyclough lot are marching up behind us. Their band leader wants a word. He always wants a word.
The band marches down the street to a cheer from the pub doorways, and plays the march for a judge nobody can see.
First prize! First! We have not been first since the 1990s! Here, love, you've earned these.

else.text: Still no drummer. Last seen getting on a boat into Standedge Tunnel. You'll find the portal up the towpath from the village.
Still no tuba. He went for a training walk on the Pennine Way and the fog came down. Look north along the flagstones.
Still no cornet. She's moping down by Dovestone Reservoir. Be kind. Be firm. Mostly be kind.
{greeting} Whit Friday's tonight and I've a band of three, a tea urn and a man who plays the triangle. He's the urn's backup.
Every village from here to Mossley holds a contest. Bands march into each one in turn and play for a judge who can't see them. We need a full band.
Our cornet is sulking at Dovestone. Our tuba is lost on the Pennine Way. Our drummer went into Standedge Tunnel on a boat trip and hasn't come out. Fetch them for me?
You're a star. Mind, the tuba's stubborn. Take him something that reminds him where he is.

band_tealady.text: {greeting} Tea's stewed, buns are fresh, and you're not a band member until you've burnt your tongue on the urn.
Brass bands used to be the mill's band, or the pit's. Now we're the village's. Same hymns, better trousers.
